cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Who Cares More?
cards.instruction: Turn every favor, memory, sacrifice, and affectionate gesture into evidence that you care more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. I kept twelve tickets from our trips. How many did you keep?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: None. I made you that album instead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. And I kept it. Your care is safe because of mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Open it. I put all my tickets inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm preserving both our collections. Let me get it a waterproof cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For a wedding cake, we weigh the flour. Please put that mug down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's quicker. I've used three mugs already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Show me the mug, and I'll weigh one mugful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used three different mugs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Please fetch all three. Apparently we're measuring the crockery before we can measure the flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm tuning this piano. Please leave the keys alone while I listen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm checking the sticky ones so you can fix those too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Mark them with these little stickers. Silently, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. Shall I peel them off so you can play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One at a time. After I reach each key. We've nearly invented a system.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Open it. I put all my tickets inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm preserving both our collections. Let me get it a waterproof cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry the heavier bag. I care more about your back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me take it for a while.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'd appear to care more about mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could share it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if I take the side with the books.

cards.title: Still a Good Sign
cards.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Our first dinner since the breakup, and you still groan at my waiter joke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I hoped you'd retired it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. You remembered. We've still got our little traditions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we eat in silence? I don't want another awful joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still know how to ask me for what you need. I'll order dessert so we have time.

cards.title: Affectionate Resentment
cards.instruction: Remain warm and familiar while letting old resentment sharpen beneath every caring gesture.

beats.speaker: B

beats.text: Yes, let's reconnect. I'll come for dinner and leave at ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to discuss why you left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Put that before pudding so we finish on something nice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if I'm still upset at ten?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll book another dinner. I want us to keep seeing each other without either evening running over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd love a weekend to patch things up. Separate rooms, though, and no old arguments.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The old arguments are why we need the weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's start with a pleasant afternoon. We can rebuild from there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't fit everything I need to say into an afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the rest by email. I'll read it when I'm ready, and we can keep the afternoon for us.
